items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the retirement and social security law, in relation to providing for the automatic enrollment for employees whose right to membership has been made optional by the head of the public retirement system involved
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5634

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the retirement and social security
law, in relation to providing for the automatic enrollment for
employees whose right to membership has been made optional by the head
of the public retirement system involved

 PURPOSE :

To provide for automatic enrollment to all pension eligible employees.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one of the bill amends § 45 of the retirement and social
security law to require employers who hire eligible employees with an
optional right to membership in a public retirement system to, after
90 days of employment, automatically enroll eligible employees who
neither affirmatively elect to join nor affirmatively elect to opt-out
of the public retirement system. The employer would be required to
provide written notice to new eligible employees that states, in
addition to their right to membership in a public retirement system,
that they will be automatically enrolled after 90 days unless the
employee opts out.

This section would not modify the right of eligible employees to join
a public retirement system as of the first date of covered employment,
but rather it creates a 90-day window for an eligible employee to
opt-out before he or she is automatically enrolled in the system.
Eligible employees who opt-out during this period would.  retain the
right to join at a later date. Employees who are mandated members of a
public retirement system are not affected by this bill, and cannot
opt-out.

This section also requires that all current eligible employees who are
not yet enrolled in a public retirement system be enrolled by
employers on October 1, 2018, unless any such current eligible
employees affirmatively opt-out of the public retirement system by
September 30, 2018. Automatic enrollment in a public retirement system
would not waive any of the eligibility requirements for previous
service credit.

Section two of the bill provides the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Currently, part-time or temporary  employees, or employees not
required to take a civil service exam, even though eligible for
membership in the public retirement system, are maintained in a
category of workers only allowed optional enrollment.  Although the
law requires employers to notify them of their optional eligibility at
the time of employment, these workers often continue to work for many
years without affirmatively enrolling in the system, thereby missing
years' worth of benefits and the financial security those benefits
should have provided in retirement.

It is not unusual to learn the story of many employees who each day
provide vital public services alongside co-workers who are covered by
a full pension only to discover, after many years on the job, that
they missed their opportunity to enroll and end up losing time earned
pension benefits when they register many years after entering the
system.This class of public employees loses valuable pension benefits
with some of them never knowing that they were entitled to a pension
plan that could have provided economic assistance which often leaves
them impoverished when they can no longer work.


It is unjust that due to a lack of information or awareness, benefits
deriving from years of public service are stolen away from employees
that have dedicated their lives to the state and local governments.
By allowing for automatic enrollment unless a worker affirmatively
opts out, all workers who are eligible will be provided the
opportunity to benefit from their retirement plan as intended, and
that this class of workers are not left pension-less due to an
innocent error at the onset of their service.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

To be determined.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
July 1, 2018.

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the retirement and social security law, in relation to providing for the automatic enrollment for employees whose right to membership has been made optional by the head of the public retirement system involved
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5634A

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the retirement and social security law, in relation to
providing for the automatic enrollment for employees whose right to
membership has been made optional by the head of the public retirement
system involved

 PURPOSE :

To provide for automatic enrollment to all pension eligible employees.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one of the bill amends § 45 of the retirement and social
security law to require employers who hire eligible employees with an
optional right to membership in the Board of Education retirement
system to, after 90 days of employment, automatically enroll eligible
employees who neither affirmatively elect to join nor affirmatively
elect to opt-out of the public retirement system. The employer would
be required to provide written notice to new eligible employees that
states, in addition to their right to membership in the Board of
Education retirement system, that they will be automatically enrolled
after 90 days unless the employee opts out.

This section would not modify the right of eligible employees to join
a public retirement system as of the first date of covered employment,
but rather it creates a 90-day window for an eligible employee to
opt-out before he or she is automatically enrolled in the system.
Eligible employees who opt-out during this period would retain the
right to join at a later date. Employees who are mandated members of a
public retirement system are not affected by this bill, and cannot
opt-out.

This section also requires that all current eligible employees who are
not yet enrolled in a public retirement system be enrolled by
employers on October 1, 2018, unless any such current eligible
employees affirmatively opt-out of the public retirement system by
September 30, 2018. Automatic enrollment in a public retirement system
would not waive any of the eligibility requirements for previous
service credit.

Section two of the bill provides the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Currently, part-time, temporary, or those employees not required to
take a civil service exam (even though eligible for membership in the
Board of Education retirement system) are maintained in a category of
workers only allowed optional enrollment.  Although the law requires
employers to notify them of their optional eligibility at the time of
employment, these workers often continue to work for many years
without affirmatively enrolling in the system, thereby missing years'
worth of benefits and the financial security those benefits should
have provided in retirement.

Under the current optional enrollment rules, only 72% of eligible
employees eventually join BERS. Of those who have not elected to
enroll in the system, approximately 73% are female with an average age
of 34.9 years old, an average salary of approximately $25,500, and an
average of 2.4 years of past service where retirement benefits were
not accruing.

It is not unusual to learn the story of many employees who each day
provide vital public services alongside co-workers who are covered by
a full pension only to discover, after many years on the job, that
they missed their opportunity to enroll and end up losing time earned
pension benefits when they register many years after entering the
system. This class of public employees loses valuable pension benefits
with some of them never knowing that they were entitled to a pension
plan that could have provided economic assistance which often leaves
them impoverished when they can no longer work.

It is unjust that due to a lack of awareness, benefits deriving from
years of public service are stolen away from employees that have
dedicated their lives to the state and local governments. By allowing
for automatic enrollment unless a worker affirmatively opts out, all
workers who are eligible will be provided the opportunity to benefit
from their retirement plan as intended, and that this class of workers
are not left pension-less due to an innocent error at the onset of
their service.

This bill does not create a new class of retirement system member;
rather it adjusts the timetable for enrollment. Once a new employee is
hired they would automatically be enrolled in the pension system 90
days after commencement of employment. This change would eliminate the
need for any refunds, and the employee would still have the right to
join the pension system immediately upon employment. This is an
efficient implementation of automatic pension enrollment.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

The New York City Office of the Actuary has estimated that the
additional annual employer contribution will be $11.0 million if no
prior years of services are purchased back by employees and $18.1
million if all years of prior service eligible for buyback are
purchased.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
July 1, 2018.

summary: Relates to employer's duties regarding optional public retirement systems; provides for the automatic enrollment for employees whose right to membership has been made optional by the head of the public retirement system involved.
